subtitle: Elephants, Inscriptions and the Making of a Warrior-King

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a war-elephant rearing against a stormy sky, with Sripurusha standing beside its massive head, hand on its tusk
panels.action: Sripurusha Permanadi stands calm at the shoulder of a towering war-elephant on a windswept ridge, the misty passes of southern Karnataka stretching behind them like a stone sea.

dialogue.text: In the age of Pallavas and Chalukyas, Sripurusha of Gangavadi is hailed both as conqueror of passes and master of elephants—how did a science of beasts shape the fate of a kingdom?

i18n.hi: पल्लवों-चालुक्यों के दौर में गंगावाड़ी का श्रीपुरुष घाट जीतने वाला, हाथियों का उस्ताद कहलाया—जानवरों की विद्या ने एक राज्य की किस्मत कैसे बदली?

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye view over the rugged hills and valleys of southern Karnataka at dawn
panels.action: The first light of dawn washes over forested hills, rocky outcrops and narrow mountain passes, with faint paths snaking through the terrain toward a distant plain.

dialogue.text: Long before Shravanabelagola’s hill became a pilgrim landmark, these hills of Gangavadi guarded the southern routes between Pallava Kanchipuram and the Deccan plains.

i18n.hi: श्रवणबेलगोला की पहाड़ी तीर्थ बनने से बहुत पहले, गंगावाड़ी की ये पहाड़ियां पल्लव कांचीपुरम और दक्खन के मैदानों के बीच दक्षिणी राहों की रखवाली करती थीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a stone inscription slab half-buried in earth, letters sharply carved
panels.action: A weathered stone inscription stands beside a village path, its old Kannada script crisp under a film of moss, while dry leaves gather at its base.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, stone records from Nanjangud and the Nandi Hills still whisper a name—Sripurusha, the Permanadi—chief among the Western Gangas of Gangavadi.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद भी, नंजनगुड और नंदी पहाड़ियों के शिलालेख एक नाम फुसफुसाते हैं—श्रीपुरुष, परमाऩदि—गंगावाड़ी के पश्चिमी गंगाओं का अगुआ।

panels.shot: interior mid-shot in a dim palace hall, focused on a young prince with scrolls and elephant miniatures
panels.action: A younger Sripurusha sits cross-legged in a lamp-lit hall, palm-leaf manuscripts and small carved elephant figurines spread before him as he studies with quiet intensity.

dialogue.text: Born into this hill kingdom in the eighth century, Sripurusha grew amid talk of Pallava raids, Chalukya counters, and the heavy tread of elephants on forest paths.

i18n.hi: आठवीं सदी में इन्हीं पहाड़ियों के राज्य में जन्मा श्रीपुरुष, पल्लव धावों, चालुक्य जवाबों और जंगल-पगडंडियों पर गूंजते हाथियों के पैर बीच बड़ा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sripurusha observing an elephant enclosure from behind a wooden fence
panels.action: Sripurusha stands by a sturdy wooden palisade watching a small herd of elephants being bathed in a river bend, trainers guiding them with long poles and soft commands.

dialogue.text: In many courts, elephants were symbols; in Gangavadi’s ravines, they were tools of war. Tradition remembers Sripurusha not just as their rider, but as a student of their craft.

i18n.hi: कई दरबारों में हाथी बस निशान थे; गंगावाड़ी की खाइयों में वे जंग के औजार थे। परंपरा श्रीपुरुष को केवल सवार नहीं, उनके हुनर का शागिर्द मानती है।

panels.shot: close-up on Sripurusha’s hand running along an elephant’s trunk, its eye watching him
panels.action: Sripurusha reaches out to rest his palm on the trunk of a calm elephant, its eye dark and steady, while a mahout looks on with a hint of surprise.

dialogue.text: Later Gajashastra traditions speak of a disciplined ‘science’ of elephants—capture, breeding, training, care, and battle. Whether or not he penned a manual, Sripurusha ruled in their shadow.

i18n.hi: बाद के गजशास्त्र हाथियों की सधा ‘विद्या’ का ज़िक्र करते हैं—पकड़, प्रजनन, सिखावन, देखभाल और रणकला। उसने ग्रंथ लिखा या नहीं, पर वह उनके साये में राज करता रहा।

panels.shot: map-like overhead shot morphing into marching armies at the Pallava frontier
panels.action: The terrain of southern India appears like a relief map, lines showing the Pallava realm to the east and rival powers to the north, while miniature armies march along the passes into Gangavadi.

dialogue.text: His reign unfolded during the long rivalry of Pallavas and Chalukyas. Gangavadi, between Kanchipuram and the Deccan, became a corridor coveted and contested.

i18n.hi: उसका राज पल्लवों और चालुक्यों की लम्बी रस्साकशी के बीच बीता। कांचीपुरम और दक्खन के बीच की गंगावाड़ी हर किसी के लिए लालच और लड़ाई की गलियारा बनी।

panels.shot: commanding wide shot of Sripurusha in armor atop a hill, overlooking a narrow pass with troops assembling
panels.action: Armored and bareheaded, Sripurusha stands at the brink of a rocky ledge, gazing down at a narrow mountain pass where his infantry, cavalry and elephants gather in ordered ranks.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions are terse. They speak of a Permanadi who ‘strengthened the Gangas’, who held the passes, and won renown on the Pallava frontier.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख कम बोलते हैं। बस बताते हैं उस परमाऩदि को जिसने ‘गंगों को मजबूत किया’, घाटियां थामीं और पल्लव सीमा पर यश पाया।

panels.shot: mid-shot in a council tent, Sripurusha and generals leaning over a palm-leaf map
panels.action: Inside a large canvas tent, Sripurusha and his commanders crouch over a palm-leaf map weighed down with stones, tiny elephant figurines marking key points along the passes.

dialogue.speaker: sripurusha
dialogue.text: “The pass is narrow; let our elephants be the wall,”

i18n.hi: “घाट तंग है; हमारे हाथी ही दीवार बनें।”

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle wide of an elephant corps advancing slowly through a forested pass
panels.action: An orderly column of elephants, armor-clad and trunk-chained, advances carefully along a forested ridge path, Sripurusha riding the lead elephant, dense foliage brushing their flanks.

dialogue.text: Elephant corps were not blunt hammers alone. Deployed with care in such passes, they blocked routes, guarded baggage, and carried the king’s presence where horses feared to tread.

i18n.hi: हाथी-दल सिर्फ कुंद हथौड़ा नहीं था। ऐसे संकरे घाटों में सोच-समझकर उतारे जाएं तो राह रोकें, रसद बचाएं और वहां तक राजा की उपस्थिति ले जाएं जहां घोड़े भी कांपें।

panels.shot: tense medium-wide in a foggy pass as Sripurusha halts his column, listening
panels.action: In a mist-filled defile, Sripurusha raises his hand to halt the elephant column, his face intent as distant drums echo faintly from beyond a bend.

dialogue.text: The sources do not paint each battle. They leave us instead with titles, hints of clashes near the Nandi Hills, and the knowledge that he emerged as the strongman of his line.

i18n.hi: स्रोत हर जंग नहीं दिखाते। बस उपाधियां छोड़ते हैं, नंदी पहाड़ियों के आस-पास की झड़पों के इशारे, और ये तथ्य कि वह अपनी कुल का लौह-पुरुष बनकर उभरा।

panels.shot: dramatic long shot of opposing forces facing each other across a valley floor, elephants on both sides
panels.action: Two armies face each other across a wide valley, ranks of spearmen and archers behind lines of elephants, with Sripurusha visible on a central elephant, spear in hand, as clouds gather overhead.

dialogue.text: Some later traditions claimed great victories over Pallava arms; scholars read the record cautiously, seeing a Ganga king who survived and consolidated in a dangerous neighbourhood.

i18n.hi: बाद की कथाओं ने पल्लव सेनाओं पर भारी जीतें लिखीं; विद्वान शांति से पढ़ते हैं—उन्हें एक गंग राजा दिखता है जिसने खतरनाक मोहल्ले में बचकर राज जमाया।

panels.shot: close-up profile of Sripurusha atop his elephant just before engagement, wind tugging his hair
panels.action: Sripurusha stands steady on the howdah of his war-elephant, eyes narrowed toward the enemy lines, as a gust of wind stirs his hair and the banner behind him.

dialogue.speaker: sripurusha
dialogue.text: “A king who cannot read beasts cannot read men.”

i18n.hi: “जो जानवरों को नहीं पढ़ सकता, वो इंसानों को क्या समझेगा।”

panels.shot: suggestive wide shot of armies clashing from a distance, dust clouds rising, without close violence
panels.action: From a distant hillside, the viewer sees lines of warriors and elephants meet in the valley, dust plumes rising and banners swaying, while Sripurusha’s elephant pushes forward at the center.

dialogue.text: War in this age was close and harsh, but our lens remains the stone record: that under Sripurusha, Gangavadi did not fall; it endured and even claimed new honours.

i18n.hi: इस युग की जंग पास से, कड़ी थी; पर हमारा शीशा वही पत्थर-लिपि है: कि श्रीपुरुष के रहते गंगावाड़ी टूटी नहीं—टिकी रही और नए मान-सम्मान भी जीते।

panels.shot: quiet medium shot after battle, Sripurusha dismounting to inspect resting elephants in camp at dusk
panels.action: At dusk in a quiet camp, Sripurusha steps down from his elephant, touching its flank as it rests, while grooms fan the animals and apply herbal pastes to their legs.

dialogue.text: Elephant science did not end when trumpets fell silent. It meant treating wounds, easing strain, choosing rest over glory when the animals’ limits were reached.

i18n.hi: हाथियों का विज्ञान रण-नगाड़े थमने पर भी खत्म नहीं होता। इसमें घाव भरना, थकान घटाना, और जानवर की हद पर शौहरत नहीं, आराम चुनना भी शामिल था।

panels.shot: interior shot of a royal chamber where Sripurusha listens to a scholar reciting from a palm-leaf manuscript
panels.action: In a polished stone chamber, Sripurusha sits on a low throne as a scholar stands before him, reading from a palm-leaf manuscript, a painted elephant diagram visible on a board nearby.

dialogue.text: Courtly texts on elephants were part of statecraft, like treatises on law or astronomy. To patronise such knowledge was to arm the kingdom as surely as forging spears.

i18n.hi: दरबारी गजशास्त्र राज्य-कला का हिस्सा थे, जैसे धर्म या ज्योतिष के ग्रंथ। ऐसी विद्या को सहारा देना उतना ही हथियार था, जितना नई भालें गढ़ना।

panels.shot: serene wide shot of Shravanabelagola hill and tank in the distance under a clear sky
panels.action: The rocky hill of Shravanabelagola rises above a tranquil tank, stepped ghats leading to the water, with a few early shrines visible along the slope under a clear blue sky.

dialogue.text: While later Gangas became famed for Jain endowments at Shravanabelagola, Sripurusha’s legacy lay in making such patronage possible—by first securing the land and the routes.

i18n.hi: बाद के गंग राजा श्रवणबेलगोला के जैन दान के लिए मशहूर हुए; पर श्रीपुरुष की धरोहर वही नींव थी—ज़मीन और राहें पहले सुरक्षित करना।

panels.shot: close-up of another inscription being carved, chisel and hammer mid-strike, letters forming his title
panels.action: A stonecutter’s hand holds a chisel against a fresh slab as a hammer descends, newly carved letters spelling out a royal title while stone dust hangs in the air.

dialogue.text: His titles—Permanadi and more—travelled on copper plates and stone. They do not recount each decision, but they signal how contemporaries ranked his strength among southern kings.

i18n.hi: उसकी उपाधियां—परमाऩदि वगैरह—ताम्रपत्रों और पत्थरों पर चल पड़ीं। हर फैसला नहीं बतातीं, पर दिखाती हैं कि समकालीन दक्षिणी राजाओं की निगाह में उसकी ताकत कहां ठहरती थी।

panels.shot: final contemplative medium-wide of an older Sripurusha walking alongside a young elephant at sunrise
panels.action: An older Sripurusha, features lined but posture firm, walks slowly beside a young elephant along a ridge path at sunrise, both silhouettes framed against the brightening sky.

dialogue.text: Today, Sripurusha stands at the meeting of inscription and lore—a ruler who used a science of elephants to hold narrow passes, reminding us that in every age, knowledge is a weapon as real as steel.

i18n.hi: आज श्रीपुरुष शिलालेख और कथा के मोड़ पर खड़ा है—वह राजा जिसने हाथियों की विद्या से संकरे घाट थामे, याद दिलाते हुए कि हर युग में ज्ञान, इस्पात जितना सच्चा हथियार होता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Elephants, Inscriptions and the Making of a Warrior-King
subtitle_i18n.hi: हाथी, शिलालेख और एक योद्धा-राजा का जन्म
